what: campaign_v8 is showing plateau signals at ~cycle 60. Diagnosing WHICH ceiling it is, because v7's ceiling was the OBJECTIVE and the fix was a new loss -- repeating that move here would be wrong. The evidence says v8 is DATA-limited.
headline: v8's ceiling is data, not objective and not capacity. Do not answer it with another loss-function change.

the_plateau_signals.caveat: 8-cycle windows; the val WDL move is 0.0014 nats and would be noise alone. What makes it worth acting on is four unrelated indicators turning together.

the_diagnosis_data_limited.method: Compare training loss to held-out loss. A large and widening gap with early overfitting means the model has exhausted its data, not its capacity or its objective.
why_this_says_DATA: The 0.036 nat generalisation gap is roughly the same size as train loss's entire distance from the label-entropy floor (~0.5547). The model fits its rows and generalises materially worse.
EPOCHS=1 already, and in 38% of cycles even ONE epoch on 4.4M rows made held-out loss worse (best_epoch=0). There is no safe amount of training left to do on this data.
train_samples is flat at ~4.41M and has been for the whole retained window. The replay window is not growing, so each cycle re-trains on nearly the same distribution.
Capacity is NOT the constraint: a capacity-limited model would show train and val loss both stuck and CLOSE together. These are stuck and FAR apart.

why_this_matters_the_wrong_fix_is_tempti.v7_ceiling: OBJECTIVE saturation. BCE through sigmoid(cp/400) lost gradient exactly where a strengthening net put its evaluations. Fixed by adding a cp-space Huber term and restoring the outcome signal -- a loss-function change, and it worked (4 acceptances in 61 cycles vs v7's 1 in 28 at the equivalent stage).
why_this_matters_the_wrong_fix_is_tempti.v8_ceiling: DATA. Overfitting within a single epoch on a fixed 4.4M-row window.
why_this_matters_the_wrong_fix_is_tempti.the_trap: The natural move after a successful v7->v8 objective fix is another objective fix. That would not address overfitting on a static corpus. More capacity and more epochs are also ruled out by the same evidence -- epochs are already at 1 and still too many 38% of the time.

converging_evidence_from_unrelated_direc: Pipeline profiling (2026-08-16): the cycle is TEACHER-RELABEL-bound at 47%, with self-play only 15%. The constraint on data volume is the cost of LABELLING positions, not generating them. Raising SELFPLAY_GAMES scales relabel too, so it buys only ~23% more games/day for a 62% longer cycle.
Corpus economics: the field trains on 1e9-1e10 rows; PieBot uses ~4.3M per generation and ~695k fresh positions per cycle.
The standing audit independently called eval/datagen the harder half of the remaining gap.

do_not: Start a v9 with a new objective. That was the v7->v8 fix and it does not address this ceiling.
Raise EPOCHS or hidden width. Both are contraindicated by the same measurement.
Raise SELFPLAY_GAMES alone. Relabel scales with it; measured to buy ~23% for a 62% longer cycle.
do: Treat data VOLUME and DIVERSITY as the binding constraint. That is a hardware and storage decision, not a code change.
Consider whether the replay window (6 cycles) is recycling too narrow a distribution -- a wider window costs disk, which is the same constraint.

Revisit the teacher-relabel cost, since it is what caps throughput. Note that TEACHER_SAMPLE_FRACTION going to 1.0 was one of the two changes that jointly installed v7's ceiling, so cutting it back is NOT a free throughput win and needs its own lineage.
what_to_do.trigger_to_act: 25 cycles without an acceptance, or val WDL still rising at cycle 70. At cycle 61 the gap is 20.

caveats: 8 retained cycles; older ones were pruned by retention, so the gap trend cannot be extended backwards to v8's start.
The gap slope (+0.000142/cycle) is small and rests on 8 points. The harder evidence is the best_epoch=0 rate, which is a discrete outcome rather than a trend fit.
train_loss_history[0] is the loss after the single training epoch, not a per-step curve, so 'overfitting within one epoch' is inferred from best_epoch=0 rather than observed mid-epoch.
A single further acceptance would falsify the plateau reading. v8's own history is quiet stretches punctuated by real steps -- cycle 26 was +21.6 Elo.

the_one_lever_that_needs_no_new_hardware.rationale: train_samples is 4.41M because the window is 6 cycles x ~695k fresh rows. Widening the window is the only way to increase rows-per-training-pass without more hardware, and rows-per-pass is exactly what the widening 0.036 nat generalisation gap says is short.

costs_measured.fresh_rows_per_day: UNCHANGED -- self-play rate is identical; only the training pass sees more

the_one_lever_that_needs_no_new_hardware.why_the_staleness_objection_does_not_app: The relabel teacher is `active_model`, which advances ONLY on gate acceptance. The last acceptance was cycle 41, 20 cycles ago, so every row from cycle 41 onward was labelled by the same net. Widening 6 -> 12 adds ZERO teacher staleness. The plateau that motivates the change is also what makes it safe -- and this argument EXPIRES the moment a new model is accepted.
the_one_lever_that_needs_no_new_hardware.not_a_lineage_change: REPLAY_WINDOW_CYCLES is not part of objective_metadata (schema, target_schema, loss_kind, target_cp, teacher_mix, max_teacher_cp, outcome_decay, min_teacher_depth, huber_delta_cp, wdl_scale_cp, cp_loss_weight), so this does NOT require a fresh OUT_ROOT or a weights-only bootstrap. It is an in-lineage config change.
deployment_constraints: RETAIN_FULL_CYCLES must exceed REPLAY_WINDOW_CYCLES or replay silently shrinks when retention deletes cycles -- the launcher enforces this with a die().
Must land at a TRUE cycle boundary: a supervisor restart re-runs the entire in-flight cycle from self-play, ~23 min.
Reversible: set the values back and restart.
the_one_lever_that_needs_no_new_hardware.expected_effect_and_how_to_falsify_it: If the ceiling is data, doubling rows-per-pass should NARROW the train/val gap from ~0.036 and reduce the best_epoch=0 rate from 38%. If the gap and the no-op rate are unchanged after ~10 cycles, the data hypothesis is wrong and the 23% throughput was spent for nothing -- revert.
the_one_lever_that_needs_no_new_hardware.status: ANALYSED AND COSTED, NOT DEPLOYED. Awaiting a decision, because it trades 23% of training throughput for data volume on a live production run.
